name: Danazol

lead: Danazol is an oral steroid prescribed for endometriosis, hereditary angioedema and some blood disorders. It has weak androgenic effects.
It has no studied role in appearance; mentions in muscle communities relate to its hormonal effects, not trials.

paras: It suppresses LH and FSH, blocks several steroid-making enzymes and displaces hormones from SHBG, raising free testosterone. It also binds the androgen receptor.
Acne, hair growth, weight gain, lipid changes, liver enzyme elevation and permanent voice deepening are reported. It is contraindicated in pregnancy and prescription-only.

lead: Danazol is an oral synthetic steroid derived from ethisterone. It has weak androgenic and anabolic activity, along with antigonadotropic, progestogenic and functional antioestrogenic effects. It is a prescription drug used mainly for endometriosis, with approved or off-label use in hereditary angioedema, fibrocystic breast disease and some blood disorders [1][2].

It was synthesised in 1963 at Sterling Winthrop and approved by the US FDA in the 1970s as the first drug specifically indicated for endometriosis; it has since been largely replaced for that purpose by GnRH analogues, which cause fewer masculinising effects [1]. Its androgenic effects include acne, excess hair growth and irreversible voice deepening in women [1].

Danazol has no established role in appearance enhancement, and no studies of it for that purpose were found. Its blood-disorder uses, such as telomere diseases, are the subject of ongoing clinical research.

paras: Danazol is used for endometriosis, and is approved in the US for symptomatic fibrocystic breast disease and for preventing attacks of hereditary angioedema [1][2]. Off-label uses described include heavy menstrual bleeding, immune thrombocytopenia and systemic lupus erythematosus [1]. As of recent guidance, newer targeted therapies have made it a second-line option for hereditary angioedema prophylaxis [2].

Androgenic effects such as acne, hirsutism, weight gain and voice deepening can occur, along with unfavourable blood lipid changes, liver enzyme elevation and mood changes. It is contraindicated in pregnancy because it can virilise a female fetus, and liver function monitoring is advised during long-term therapy [1][2]. Wikipedia also notes links to benign liver tumours and, in endometriosis patients, to ovarian cancer risk [1].

Danazol suppresses the mid-cycle surge of LH and FSH, inhibits several steroidogenic enzymes, and binds sex hormone-binding globulin, raising free testosterone levels. It binds strongly to the androgen receptor and more weakly to progesterone, glucocorticoid and oestrogen receptors [1][2]. Oral bioavailability is low and increases with food; it is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4 [1].

A 1976 double-blind study in nine patients with hereditary angioedema found only one attack during 46 danazol courses versus 44 attacks in 47 placebo courses, with increases in C1 esterase inhibitor and C4 [3]. A 2016 trial in patients with telomere diseases reported effects on telomere length and blood counts [4]. Small registered trials have also examined it in immune thrombocytopenia, Fanconi anaemia, dyskeratosis congenita and other conditions [5][6]. No studies were found of danazol for appearance or physique.

Danazol is prescription-only in the countries listed above. It is also sold in some places under many brand names, and one veterinary brand exists [1]. Within bodybuilding circles it is sometimes mentioned for its effect on sex hormone-binding globulin and free testosterone, but this community use is not documented by clinical studies.
